item.content:encoded:
At Travel-Dealz, we regularly feature round-the-world building blocks: cheap one-way tickets that you can combine into your very own trip around the world. Sometimes several opportunities come together at the same time and fit nicely into one itinerary.

If you book four flights separately, you can currently explore several cities in North America and Asia on a single trip, starting at €860. We cover the short gaps in between by bus and train (already included in the price). Above all, though, this article is meant to show what’s possible. You can of course adapt our example routing as you like and add more stops in America and Asia… or skip the US entirely.

Many of these building blocks are only this cheap until spring (March, April 2027 at the latest). That isn’t exactly the ideal time to visit the Pacific Northwest. We’d recommend adding at least one checked bag on every flight so you’re prepared for all climate zones. With at least 20 kg of luggage on all segments, you’ll pay €933 in total.

Info

Accommodation, airport transfers, etc. are not included. You’ll also have to pay the following fees to the border authorities:

  • Canada: approx. CA$7 (~€4) for the eTA
  • USA: approx. US$40 (~€36) for the ESTA + US$30 (~€27) for the I-94 (required when entering by land)

Example Route: 6 Cities on 3 Continents

Our example route takes you to a total of 6 cities in 6 different countries. With a layover (max. 24 hours) in China, you even get a chance to get a taste of one more country.

First, you take the train from Frankfurt to Paris. From there, you fly on to Vancouver (or Calgary). You cross the US border by train before the flight to Singapore: at 17 hours, by far the longest one on this trip. Then you continue overland to Kuala Lumpur. The rest of the journey is by plane again: first to Hanoi in Vietnam and from there back to Frankfurt.

Here’s a quick overview of the individual segments:

Below you’ll find more information on each leg:

Part 1: Frankfurt – Paris for €40

Since the long-haul flight departs from Paris, you first need to get to France. For once, we’re not going for the budget option (FlixBus from €28 or a cheap TGV from Strasbourg from €18), but the ICE directly from Frankfurt. If you book early enough, fares start at €39.99 for the 4-hour ride.

Show Deal

We recommend staying at least one day in Paris, as getting there on the same day is cutting it close with a 1 pm departure. Besides, Paris is always worth a visit and a great start to your trip around the world.

Part 2: Paris – Vancouver for €263

Not quite as cheap as in the opposite direction, but still one of the cheapest options from Europe to North America: WestJet flies you from Paris to Calgary from €199, or on to Vancouver from €263. In February, expect temperatures of around 0 to 10 °C there.

Show Deal

Availability: until mid-March 2027 (Google Flights)

The fare only includes hand luggage and a personal item. A checked bag of up to 23 kg costs around €50 extra via Trip.com* or directly with WestJet (included with Delta SkyMiles status).

Alternative

Alternative 1: Fly to Victoria (the capital of British Columbia) instead of Vancouver for the same price. From there, you can continue to Seattle via Port Angeles, USA for around €30. Of course, you can also easily combine Vancouver and Victoria.

Alternative 2: Fly nonstop from Paris to Calgary from €199 and, after a few days there, book your own onward flight to Vancouver, for example.

Part 3: Vancouver – Seattle for €31

The most comfortable way to get to the US is by Amtrak. The ride on the Amtrak Cascades takes around four hours. The website shows a travel time of 5 hours, apparently because it gets confused by the time change. Price: from US$34 (~€30). FlixBus is an alternative at the same price.

Show Deal

Availability: all year round, without major price fluctuations

The weather in Seattle will probably be just as cold and grey as in Vancouver. At least that has one upside: hotels are much cheaper than in high season.

Part 4: Seattle – Singapore for €266

On the next flight, you can finally take off your winter coat and stash it at the bottom of your suitcase. Temperatures between 25 and 30 °C await you in Singapore. The flight is nonstop, but still takes a whopping 17 hours.

Show Deal

Availability: until May 2027 (Google Flights)

Once you’ve had enough of Singapore, you can take a day trip to Batam (about an hour by ferry). And sooner or later, head on to Malaysia.

Part 5: Singapore – Kuala Lumpur for €20

The detour to Malaysia is by no means a must. If you prefer, you can also fly directly from Singapore to Vietnam from €75. But when you’re already in the area, why not add another country in Southeast Asia?

From Singapore, a long-distance bus takes you to Kuala Lumpur for around €20. For a small surcharge, you can also choose a bus with business or first class seats. The exact luggage rules vary by operator.

Show Deal

Availability: all year round

Alternative

Take the KTM shuttle across the border from Singapore to Johor Bahru for around €3. From there, continue to Kuala Lumpur with Malaysia’s national railway for around €17.

Part 6: Kuala Lumpur – Hanoi for €65

Malaysia is a great place to treat yourself – hotels in particular are much cheaper than in Singapore. If you like, you can also visit other destinations in Malaysia from Kuala Lumpur, such as the island of Langkawi (domestic flights from €50 round trip).

In our example trip, you continue directly from Kuala Lumpur to Vietnam. A ticket to Hanoi costs €65 (with 7 kg of hand luggage). With 20 kg of checked luggage, it’s €88 if you book directly with AirAsia.

Show Deal

Availability: all year round

Alternative

Fly to Da Nang, Phu Quoc, Ho Chi Minh City, … for the same price and spend more time in Vietnam. Or add another stop in Thailand, Cambodia, … There are plenty of destinations for under €100.

Part 7: Hanoi – Frankfurt for €175

After the modern metropolises of Singapore and Kuala Lumpur, the hustle and bustle of Vietnam is quite a contrast. You’ll notice it the first time you try to cross the street. But all the cities in Southeast Asia have one thing in common: cheap, delicious food you’ll miss for a long time once you’re back home. So enjoy the authentic cuisine one more time before heading back to Frankfurt.

Show Deal

Availability: until March 2027

We’ve already dedicated a separate post to the cheap one-way tickets from Hanoi to Frankfurt. You can fly via Chengdu, Shanghai or Beijing. If you fly via Beijing, you might get the chance to fly on an Air China Boeing 747. Sounds like a fitting end to your trip around the world.

Editor’s Note: Three continents for €933 including checked bags on every segment. The anchor of this routing is Singapore Airlines’ 17-hour nonstop from Seattle to Singapore for just €266 – usually one of the priciest legs on any trip around the world.

Alternative: Paris, Vancouver, Tokyo, Osaka & Hanoi from €931 (€1,032 with Luggage)

With articles like this, we often get asked whether there are options that avoid the US. Yes, that’s possible – but you’ll have to tweak the routing a bit. The following example includes two stops in Japan, but skips Seattle, Singapore and Kuala Lumpur in return.

More Round-the-World Building Blocks

Looking for more ideas for your trip? Then check out the following articles. The tickets from Australia to Europe for under €300 are also very interesting, but you have to get there first. At least to/from Asia, there are also cheap business class options thanks to Turkmenistan Airlines:

One Way: €700 Scoot Premium Economy Australia → Vienna (With 30 Kg Luggage)
Round-the-World Segment: €1,509 One-Way Hainan Airlines Business Class Melbourne to Madrid (with China Stopover)

item.content:encoded:
Icelandair is currently offering cheap flights to New York. Departing from five European countries, you can fly to the “Big Apple” from just €306 round-trip. This fare includes a personal item, carry-on luggage and drinks, but no meals. If you need checked luggage, the corresponding fare is available directly from the airline from €441.

Availability can be found for travel from January to April 2027. Both the outbound and return flights connect in Reykjavik, where you can add a stopover in each direction for a surcharge (max. 78 hours on the Light fare). If you book the fare with checked luggage, you can add a stopover of up to 7 days.

Show Deal

You can fly from the following airports for less than €390:

  • Munich at €306
  • Berlin at €313
  • Frankfurt at €323
  • Stockholm at €365 (~SEK 3,989)
  • Gdansk at €373 (~PLN 1,636)
  • Zurich at €380 (~CHF 348)
  • Oslo at €384 (~NOK 4,022)
  • Bergen at €384 (~NOK 4,022)

To book, you can also use the following form and get redirected to Skyscanner* (from €306) or directly to Icelandair (from €342). We’ve marked cheap availability in green:

Subscribe to our WhatsApp Channel or Telegram Channel to get instant notifications for all of our best deals!

Between continental Europe and Iceland, Icelandair usually operates the Boeing 737 MAX with an average seat pitch of 31 inches (79 cm). From Keflavik to New York, it mostly flies the Boeing 767 in a 2-3-2 configuration (also 31 inches of seat pitch), though some connections are also operated by the Boeing 737 MAX or Airbus A321. The layovers in Iceland are usually short at around one hour each way, and the total travel time is about 11 hours.

Info

To enter the USA, you need either an ESTA for US$40 (~€36) or a visa. Please check the current entry requirements for your nationality before booking.

Search & Book

According to the fare rules, the flights can be booked until November 17, 2026 for travel in the following period:

  • January to April 2027 (excluding March)

The minimum stay is three days or a Saturday night stay. In theory, you can stay at your destination for up to 12 months. With an ESTA, however, stays are limited to a maximum of 90 days.

You can easily find suitable dates with Google Flights (guide). You can then book from €306 via Skyscanner* or from €342 directly with Icelandair.

Editor’s Note: Around €300 to €380 round-trip from Germany, Scandinavia, Poland or Switzerland to New York on a full-service airline is a solid price for winter and spring. The real bonus is Reykjavik: for just €40 more, you can turn the layover into a few days in Iceland and get two trips on one ticket.

item.content:encoded:
In April 2027, the Costa Diadema sails from Leixões (the cruise port of Porto) to Kiel on a 9-day repositioning voyage that calls at ports in Spain, France, England and Denmark.

Setting sail on Thursday, April 22, 2027, you can book this cruise starting at just €399 per person (€50 per day) in an inside cabin with full board and gratuities included. Oceanview cabins start at €519 per person, while balcony cabins are available from €639 per person (based on double occupancy). Solo travelers can book an inside cabin starting from €689 (€86 per day). The cruise ends in Kiel on Friday, April 30, 2027.

If you’d like drinks included, the All Inclusive fare (with the MyItalian drinks package) starts at €594 per person (€74 per day) in an inside cabin, or €884 for solo travelers.

Info

Do you have questions about the offer, need help booking this cruise, or are you looking for a cruise that suits you even better? Feel free to contact us via our inquiry form or WhatsApp. We’re glad to help.

To enter the United Kingdom, you need a valid passport and, for most nationalities, an Electronic Travel Authorisation (ETA), which currently costs €23 (~£19).

Show Deal

Subscribe to our WhatsApp Channel or Telegram Channel to get instant notifications for all of our best deals!

What’s Included

Costa cruise fares include the following:

  • Full board: main dining rooms and buffet restaurant (specialty restaurants cost extra)
  • Drinks: water, coffee and tea at breakfast, plus filtered tap water in the buffet during opening hours
  • Gratuities: all onboard service charges are included
  • Onboard facilities: pools, sun loungers, gym and theater shows

The cheapest prices are for the Light fare, which gets you a guarantee cabin: Costa assigns your cabin number, and changes are limited. If you want to choose your cabin, the flexible MyCruise fare starts at €579 per person (€72 per day) in an inside cabin.

Important note on drinks: Costa only includes water, coffee and tea at breakfast and from the buffet dispensers. In the main dining rooms at lunch and dinner, all drinks (including bottled water) cost extra. That’s why a drinks package is often worth it on Costa. On this sailing, the Light All Inclusive fare with the MyItalian drinks package costs only €195 more per person (about €24 per day) than the regular Light fare, which is less than you would pay for the package separately.

Costa Drinks Packages at a Glance
  1. MySoft Drinks Package
    From €23 per adult per day (children aged 4–17 pay €15 per day). Unlimited non-alcoholic drinks by the glass: coffee, tea, soft drinks, energy drinks and non-alcoholic cocktails.
  2. MyItalian Drinks Package
    €34.30 per adult per day (included in the All Inclusive fare). Draft beer, house wines by the glass, standard spirits, classic cocktails, specialty coffees, soft drinks, one 0.5-liter bottle of water per adult per day, soft-serve gelato and one free pizza per cruise at the Pummid’Oro pizzeria.
  3. MyItalian Plus Package
    €45.80 per adult per day (included for suite guests on the All Inclusive fare). Everything in MyItalian plus premium cocktails, bottled beers, unlimited 0.5-liter bottles of water, fruit juices and the in-suite minibar.

Drinks packages can be added up to 48 hours before embarkation via MyCosta.

Editor’s Note: About €50 per day with full board and gratuities is a great price for a spring repositioning cruise. It also takes you from Portugal to northern Germany with stops in Galicia, Normandy, England and Denmark on the way.

The Route

The cruise departs Leixões near Porto on April 22, 2027 at 6:00 pm, and the first port of call is Vigo. The port city is ideal for a stroll through the old town or along the waterfront. If you want to venture further, you can take an excursion along the Galician coast or to the famous pilgrimage city of Santiago de Compostela.

After a day at sea, you reach Le Havre. The city is a good base for excursions into Normandy or to Paris. Because of the distance to the French capital, an organized shore excursion is recommended for a Paris day trip. Alternatively, Le Havre itself is worth a visit for its modern architecture, harbor district and beach promenade.

On April 26, 2027, the ship calls at Dover. You can explore the famous White Cliffs and Dover Castle, or book an excursion to Canterbury or London.

Two more sea days follow before you arrive in Aarhus. Denmark’s second-largest city combines modern architecture with historic sights, and its compact center is easy to explore on foot. A walk along the harbor or through the pedestrian zone is well worth it. On April 30, 2027, you finally reach Kiel, where the cruise ends.

The Ship

The Costa Diadema was built in 2014 and is 306 meters long and 37 meters wide, with a top speed of 25 knots. Across 15 decks, she carries up to 4,947 passengers (maximum occupancy) or 3,724 passengers (double occupancy), plus 1,200 crew members.

There are 8 restaurants and 11 bars on board. On Costa, the buffet, the main dining rooms and some snacks are included in the fare. The other dining venues cost extra, and some need a reservation.

The ship has 3 pools, one of which has a retractable glass roof, plus 8 hot tubs and various activities on deck. The theater and live music in the lounges provide entertainment in the evenings, and there is a kids club for younger guests. On itineraries with many sea days, there are also craft classes, deck and lounge games, and other creative or sports activities.

For an extra charge, there is a spa and wellness area, a casino, a video game area with a Formula 1 simulator, and a shopping promenade. The official languages on board are Italian and English, and the onboard currency is the euro.

item.content:encoded:
Have you always dreamed of a truly luxurious cruise, but without paying luxury cruise line prices? Then keep reading. Norwegian Cruise Line is currently selling a one-week Caribbean cruise on the Norwegian Getaway at a very attractive price, and it gets you into the exclusive suite area The Haven.

Setting sail on Monday, November 16, 2026 from Port Canaveral (near Orlando), the cruise makes four port stops and returns on Monday, November 23, 2026. Right now, you can book a two-bedroom Haven family villa with balcony (category H6) starting at just €1,680 per person (€240 per day), based on double occupancy, with the Free at Sea package included. Solo travelers pay from €3,149 (€450 per day) for the same villa. The last two available villas are on decks 15 and 16.

Important

Norwegian Cruise Line automatically adds a crew gratuity of US$25 (~€22) per person per day to your onboard account. If you don’t agree with it, you can have the amount adjusted or removed at Guest Services on board.

Info

To enter the US, you need either an ESTA for around US$40 (~€36) or a visa.

The price drop for the family villa is very recent, so the first screen does not show the correct price yet. During booking, select category H6 and click Check Offer once, and the price will update.

Do you have questions about the offer or the booking, or are you looking for the right cruise? Get in touch via our inquiry form or WhatsApp. We are happy to advise you personally.

Subscribe to our WhatsApp Channel or Telegram Channel to get instant notifications for all of our best deals!

Included Services

Standard fares with Norwegian Cruise Line include the following:

  • Full board with all meals in the main dining rooms and the buffet restaurant
  • Coffee and tea with main meals
  • Entertainment program and events on board

Suites in The Haven also include NCL’s Free at Sea package at no extra cost. In all other categories, you can add it for an extra charge. Free at Sea includes a premium beverage package, one or more specialty dining meals, a Wi-Fi package with 150 minutes and a US$50 (~€44) shore excursion credit per cabin per port.

Editor’s Note: A two-bedroom Haven villa with butler, private restaurant and Free at Sea included for €240 per person per day is rare on a mainstream ship. If you can travel on short notice, this is an affordable way to try suite life at sea.

The Haven

The Haven is a separate area of the ship that only guests who booked a suite there can access. That is why Norwegian Cruise Line often calls it a “ship within a ship”.

Unlike the other passengers, you get these extra privileges and inclusions:

  • The Haven Courtyard: A private area, accessible only with a special keycard, with its own pool, hot tubs and loungers.
  • The Haven Lounge & Bar: An exclusive bar and lounge for Haven guests, serving premium drinks and specialty coffees.
  • Private wellness facilities: Access to a private sauna within the Haven complex.
  • 24-hour butler service: A certified suite butler can pack your luggage, serve meals and take care of daily comforts.
  • Dedicated concierge: Your own concierge helps you plan on board and ashore, booking shore excursions, spa treatments or specialty restaurants.
  • Priority logistics: Priority embarkation and disembarkation at the pier, plus priority for tender boats in port.
  • Priority access: Haven guests get reserved seating and priority access to shows and entertainment events on board.
  • The Haven Restaurant: A private gourmet restaurant serving complimentary breakfast, lunch and dinner exclusively for Haven guests.
  • White-tablecloth service: Your butler serves dishes from the Haven Restaurant menu or the extended room service menu at a fully set table in your suite.
  • Welcome gift & snacks: A bottle of sparkling wine or champagne awaits you on arrival, and room service delivers fresh gourmet canapés to your suite every evening.

Here are a few impressions of The Haven on the Norwegian Getaway:

The Route

Your cruise starts in Port Canaveral, about 90 kilometers from Orlando in Florida. The ship leaves port at 4 pm. The first stop is Great Stirrup Cay in the Bahamas. Norwegian Cruise Line’s private island is all about a classic, carefree beach day. The waters around the island are extremely clear, and an artificial snorkeling reef is ideal for watching colorful fish and marine life. Various water sports are also available.

After a day at sea, the Norwegian Getaway reaches Saint Thomas. Magens Bay, one of the best-known beaches in the Caribbean, is here. This crescent-shaped beach has turquoise water and fine white sand, perfect for relaxing. The historic capital, Charlotte Amalie, invites you to stroll through its colonial lanes and visit the historic Fort Christian. It is also a good place to pick up a souvenir or two.

Next, the ship heads for San Juan. The capital of Puerto Rico has plenty to offer visitors. Located on the north coast of this lush tropical island, San Juan was the second settlement founded by European settlers in the Caribbean. With its massive fortresses, airy plazas and Caribbean charm, the city is also a beach paradise surrounded by turquoise waters.

The last stop is Puerto Plata in the Dominican Republic. The city wins visitors over with its Victorian architecture and vibrant culture. In the old town, you can stroll down the famous, colorful Umbrella Street. A trip to the historic Spanish fortress Fortaleza de San Felipe is also worthwhile. After another day at sea and 7 nights in total, the cruise ends back in Port Canaveral.

The Ship

The Norwegian Getaway is the second ship of the Breakaway class. She was built in 2014 at the Meyer Werft shipyard in Papenburg, Germany, and was last refurbished in 2019. The ship is 326 meters long and 52 meters wide and has room for up to 3,963 passengers and 1,646 crew members, making her one of the larger ships in the Norwegian Cruise Line fleet. Her top speed is 23 knots.

The choice of restaurants is very diverse. Besides the included main dining rooms and the buffet, there are several specialty restaurants (at extra cost), such as Cagney’s Steakhouse, where you can enjoy a perfectly cooked steak with sides. Fans of Asian cuisine will love Shanghai’s Noodle Bar, and Ocean Blue serves seafood and fish in many variations.

There is plenty to do on board, including a climbing wall, the Aqua Park with water slides, a ropes course and evening shows in the theater. The bars and lounges also offer live music. The Norwegian Getaway has an outdoor promenade deck where you can take a relaxing walk with ocean views at any time.

The range of cabins is just as varied. Studio cabins were designed specifically for solo travelers, who also get exclusive access to the Studio Lounge. Luxury lovers can choose from a large selection of suites in the separate Haven area. If you are looking for peace and relaxation, the spa offers a range of massages and wellness treatments.

The January 24 sailing leaves Hamburg at 8:00 pm and, after a day at sea, calls at Zeebrugge (7:00 am to 6:00 pm), the gateway to Bruges. In Southampton (7:00 am to 7:30 pm), London is within reach. After another sea day, the MSC Preziosa returns to Hamburg on January 31 at 7:00 am.

Throughout the winter, the MSC Preziosa sails a loop between Southampton, Hamburg, Rotterdam, Cherbourg-Octeville and Le Havre, so you can also board in one of the other ports. Sometimes the itinerary is slightly different, e.g. replacing Cherbourg or Rotterdam with Zeebrugge.

The Ship

The MSC Preziosa (Fantasia class) was built at the Chantiers de l’Atlantique shipyard, entered service in 2013, and was renovated in 2016. It is 38 meters wide and 333 meters long, has 18 decks, and accommodates nearly 3,500 passengers and 1,400 crew members.

It has 2 main restaurants and a buffet restaurant. The “Galaxy” restaurant, which has interesting Asian fusion cuisine, is highly recommended as a specialty restaurant for an additional charge. Here you can not only enjoy fantastic views of the ship and surroundings but also good food. There are also 12 bars or lounges where you can enjoy beer, wine, cocktails, and soft drinks.

In addition to the spa and fitness area as well as various cultural and leisure activities, there is also a 120-meter-long waterslide.

A casino, cinema, basketball court, tennis court, outdoor jogging track, bowling alley, and four pools (one covered) offer a variety of recreational activities.

The onboard language is English, and the currency on the ship is the euro. Originally, the ship was ordered by the Libyan government but was later sold to MSC.

The cabins are at least 16 square meters in size and are equipped with a safe, air conditioning, telephone, television, and minibar.

At Flying Blue, discounted award flights are released every month. Through the Promo Awards, you can get 25% off the standard mileage rates on rotating routes.

In November, business class to New York is on sale for 45,000 miles plus around €300 to €400 in surcharges each way. At that price, however, tickets are non-refundable and come without lounge access. Business class to Beijing, Panama City and Cape Town is also discounted (from 63,750 miles + €307), as is premium economy to destinations such as Osaka (from 37,500 miles + €235).

Show Deal

Unlike the Miles & More Mileage Bargains, Promo Awards can be booked one-way for exactly half the miles.

Important Notice: Devaluation in Effect

Since September 2026, the cheapest award tickets can neither be changed nor refunded. In addition, baggage allowances have been reduced in all cabins, and business class awards on the lowest tier no longer include lounge access. Elite status members keep some of these benefits. Read more about the changes here.

Editor’s Note: New York in business class for 45,000 miles one-way is one of the cheapest ways across the Atlantic with Air France and KLM this year. Just keep in mind that the Business Light fare means no lounge and no refunds, so only book once your plans are firm.

  • Promo Awards in November 2026
    • Business Class: New York from 45,000 Miles + €317
    • Business Class: Beijing, Panama & Cape Town from 63,750 Miles + €307

Promo Awards in November 2026

The current Promo Awards are expected to be bookable through November 30, 2026. The travel period runs through April 2027 (exact dates vary by route).

You can find an overview of all discounted routes (including European short-haul flights) on the Flying Blue website. Note that taxes and surcharges are not shown there, and several listed routes can only be booked with a paid Extra subscription.

Here are this month’s highlights:

Info

All routes listed below are only examples to give you an idea of the taxes and surcharges. Promo Awards can generally be booked to and from airports all across Europe.

Business Class: New York from 45,000 Miles + €317

The most interesting redemption this month is New York for 45,000 miles in business class. You will pay at least €300 in surcharges each way, but compared to Miles & More that is still fairly moderate.

By default, the fare includes only 1x 32 kg checked bag, no lounge access, and is non-refundable. The Standard fare with 2x 32 kg, lounge access and a cancellation option (€75 fee) costs 56,250 instead of 45,000 miles.

Premium Economy for 30,000 / 37,500 Miles (+ from €227)

Redemptions in economy class and premium economy have become much less attractive since September, as the cheapest tickets in both cabins no longer include any checked baggage. Upgrading to the Standard fare (around 7,500 miles extra) solves that and also brings back the cancellation option for a €70 fee.

Search & Book

The offers are generally valid through November 30, 2026, for travel from now until April 2027. Flying Blue uses dynamic pricing, so prices can be (significantly) higher depending on the date and departure airport.

You can book the Promo Awards directly on AirFrance.com or KLM.com. If you leave the travel dates blank, the cheapest dates are shown right in the calendar, as here for Nuremberg to Osaka in premium economy:

Sometimes the search with blank dates doesn’t work and only returns an error message. We haven’t been able to spot a pattern behind it yet.

How Can I Get the Miles Quickly?

If you are short on miles, options for topping up your account quickly without flying are limited, especially for members based outside France and the Netherlands.

Flying Blue regularly sells miles at a discount. During these sales, you pay around 1.2 to 1.4 euro cents per mile, which isn’t really worth it for Promo Awards. The regular price is even above 2 cents per mile.

For more ways to get the most out of your miles, check out our Flying Blue sweet spots.

Terms & Conditions

Keep the following rules in mind when booking Flying Blue Promo Awards:

  • Online booking only: Tickets can only be booked directly on airfrance.com or klm.com. Only tickets for (unaccompanied) minors can be booked by phone, as this isn’t possible online.
  • Dynamic pricing: Not all tickets are available at the low price. Often there are only a few dates per month at the promo rate, and prices can vary (sometimes significantly) by departure airport.
  • Three fare tiers: Since September 2026, award flights come in three tiers: Light, Standard and Flex. The Light fare is non-refundable, comes with reduced baggage and possibly other restrictions – all at the same price as before (a hidden devaluation).
  • One-way or round trip: Unlike the Miles & More Mileage Bargains, the prices also apply to one-way bookings. Open-jaw itineraries aren’t possible, but you can simply book two one-ways instead.

Explora II from luxury cruise line Explora Journeys departs on January 14, 2027 from Civitavecchia near Rome for a 10-night luxury cruise through the Western Mediterranean to Barcelona. Ports of call include Amalfi, Cagliari on Sardinia, two days in Málaga and Tangier in Morocco.

Booking through us gets you an exclusive special rate: An Ocean Terrace Suite (Category OT1) is available as a guaranteed suite from just €2,840 per person – less than €300 per night! If you would like to choose your suite (we will suggest one for you), you pay from €3,205 p.p. Booking directly with Explora, the cheapest Ocean Terrace Suite currently costs at least €3,930 p.p. Solo travelers can join from €3,550, and Penthouse suites are available from €4,275 p.p.

Exclusive

The special rate (Preferred Fare) is only available when booking through Travel-Dealz. Compared to Explora’s public price, you save around €2,000 per suite depending on the category – even compared to the non-refundable full-payment fare. With us, you only need to pay a 5% deposit.

We also have more special rates for winter voyages on Explora II. If you’re interested, just get in touch and we’ll find something that suits you!

Do you have questions about the offer, need help, or are you looking for a cruise that suits you even better? Feel free to contact us via our inquiry form. We’re glad to help.

Info

You will need a valid passport to go ashore in Tangier.

Tip

If you are a member of the Explora Club with at least Silver status, you can get an additional 5% discount on the cruise fare. Explora also offers a status match, e.g. from MSC Voyagers Club!

Simply provide your membership number in the inquiry form or during the booking process. The discount will only be shown once you receive your reservation confirmation.

Subscribe to our WhatsApp Channel or Telegram Channel to get instant notifications for all of our best deals!

Included Services

As part of Explora Journeys’ all-inclusive luxury standard, the cruise fare covers the following amenities:

  • Full board dining across venues, including most specialty restaurants and 24-hour in-suite dining
  • A curated selection of fine wines and premium spirits
  • Specialty coffees, fine teas, and soft drinks (including fully stocked in-suite minibar)
  • Welcome bottle of chilled champagne upon arrival in your suite
  • One bottle of wine and one bottle of premium spirit of your choice in your suite
  • All onboard crew gratuities and service charges
  • 24-hour suite service and concierge assistance
  • Complimentary access to the Ocean Wellness Thermal Spa area
  • Complimentary port shuttle buses between ship and city centers (where available)
  • Unlimited high-speed Starlink Wi-Fi access throughout the ship

The following optional amenities and services carry an additional charge:

  • Tasting menus at the Anthology culinary concept
  • Hands-on cooking masterclasses at the Chef’s Kitchen
  • Ultra-premium reserve vintage wines, champagnes, and rare spirits
  • Individual spa and wellness treatments (massages, facials, etc.)

Editor’s Note: Under €300 per person per night for an all-inclusive Explora suite is a rare price – and around €1,100 p.p. less than booking directly. Winter in the Mediterranean won’t bring beach weather, but you’ll get the Amalfi Coast, Málaga and Tangier without the summer crowds.

The Route

Your cruise begins in Civitavecchia, Rome’s cruise port. A pre-cruise stay in the Eternal City can be well worth it in winter, without the usual crowds of tourists.

The next morning, you’ll reach Amalfi on the coast of the same name, where you’ll go ashore by tender. The small town with its Cathedral of Sant’Andrea clings to the steep cliffs, and just a few kilometers away lie Ravello with Villa Rufolo and Villa Cimbrone, as well as Positano.

Next up is Cagliari, the capital of Sardinia. From the old Castello quarter and the Bastione di Saint Remy, you’ll enjoy a great view over the city and harbor. The Roman amphitheater and Poetto beach are also worth a visit.

After a sea day, the ship docks in Cartagena, Spain. Highlights include the Roman Theater, the Castillo de la Concepción and the Modernisme façades of the old town.

You’ll then spend two days in Málaga, with the ship only departing at 23:30 on the evening of the second day. That leaves plenty of time for an excursion to the Alhambra in Granada. In Málaga itself, the Alcazaba fortress, the Roman Theater, the cathedral and the Picasso Museum await.

A special highlight of the route is the stop in Tangier, Morocco. Wander through the medina past the Petit and Grand Socco up to the Kasbah, and on a clear day enjoy a view across the Strait of Gibraltar from Café Hafa. A little outside the city lie the Caves of Hercules and Cape Spartel, while Tétouan is an option for a longer excursion.

After another sea day, Explora II makes a final call in Alicante. The Castillo de Santa Bárbara towers above the city, while below you’ll find the palm-lined Explanada de España promenade, the Barrio de Santa Cruz old town and Postiguet beach. Your cruise ends in Barcelona at 08:00 on January 24, 2027.

The Ship

Delivered in 2024 by Italy’s Fincantieri shipyard, Explora II measures 248 meters in length and 32 meters in width, carrying up to 900 guests served by 640 crew members. This exceptional 1.25:1 guest-to-crew ratio guarantees personalized, European-style luxury service throughout your voyage.

The ship’s 461 oceanfront suites and residences start at a spacious 35 m² (377 sq ft)—among the largest entry-level accommodations in the ultra-luxury cruise sector. Every suite boasts floor-to-ceiling glass windows, a private teak terrace with daybeds, and walk-in closets with a seated vanity area.

Culinary diversity is a hallmark of the experience, offering six distinct open-seating restaurants serving international gastronomy, 12 bars and lounges with unlimited premium wines and spirits, an extensive 700 m² spa with complimentary thermal area access, and three outdoor heated pools complete with private daybed cabanas.

The primary onboard language is English, and onboard purchases can be settled in Euro or US Dollar depending on the itinerary using major credit cards.

item.content:encoded:
The MSC World Europa, one of the modern flagships in the MSC Cruises fleet, departs on January 21, 2028, for a one-week Western Mediterranean voyage round-trip from Barcelona. An attractive deal is currently available for interior suites within the exclusive, all-inclusive MSC Yacht Club “ship-within-a-ship” sanctuary.

You can book a 7-night cruise in an MSC Yacht Club Interior Suite starting at €1,857 per person (€265 per day). Several other departures in January and February 2028 are also available for under €2,000 per person. Unfortunately, the deal doesn’t work for solo travelers: a single Yacht Club Interior Suite currently costs €3,602 (€515 per day), almost twice as much.

The fare includes full board dining, daily crew gratuities, and full access to the luxury privileges of the Yacht Club—most notably the top-tier Premium Extra Drink Package, 24-hour butler service, and complimentary high-speed Wi-Fi (details below in our Yacht Club benefits section).

Info

Do you have questions about the offer, need help booking this cruise, or are you looking for a cruise that suits you even better? Feel free to contact us via our inquiry form or WhatsApp. We’re glad to help.

Booking Tip

In the booking form, first select the main category Suite. This will display category YIN, which is the official code for the MSC Yacht Club Interior Suite.

Subscribe to our WhatsApp Channel or Telegram Channel to get instant notifications for all of our best deals!

In addition to the January 21 departure, the following winter 2028 sailings are currently bookable at similar rates. All prices are per person for an MSC Yacht Club Interior Suite (category YIN):

  • January 28 – February 4, 2028 from €1,857
  • January 14 – 21, 2028 from €1,937
  • February 11 – 18, 2028 from €1,957

Editor’s Note: For €265 per person per day, you get MSC’s Yacht Club “ship-within-a-ship” with butler service, Wi-Fi and the Premium Extra drink package already included. That’s what makes the interior suite worth it.

Included Services in the MSC Yacht Club

Booking a suite in the MSC Yacht Club unlocks an exclusive “ship-within-a-ship” enclave keycard-accessible only to Yacht Club guests. Perks include 24-hour dedicated butler and concierge service as well as complimentary unlimited internet access for the duration of the voyage.

Guests benefit from priority check-in and check-out, dedicated luggage handling, and exclusive dining venues. Crucially, your booking includes the top-tier Premium Extra Drink Package, covering an extensive selection of premium spirits, cocktails, wines, beers, and specialty coffees across every bar, lounge, and restaurant on the entire ship.

For relaxation, you enjoy complimentary access to the Aurea Spa Thermal Area, alongside the private Yacht Club Top Sail Lounge and an exclusive pool deck with private whirlpools, sun loungers, and poolside bar service. In your suite, you will find premium Egyptian cotton bedding, a pillow menu, luxury bathrobes, slippers, and a welcome package featuring Prosecco and artisan chocolates.

Below are impressions of the MSC Yacht Club aboard MSC World Europa:

The Route

The cruise sets sail from the Catalan capital of Barcelona. Arrive early to explore Antoni Gaudí’s architectural wonders, such as the Sagrada Família, before the ship departs at 18:00. Your first port of call is the lively French port city of Marseille, offering easy excursions to nearby Aix-en-Provence.

The journey continues along the Italian Riviera to Genoa, followed by Civitavecchia, the port gateway for day trips into Rome by regional train or organized tour. The ship then sails south to Messina on the island of Sicily, where you can explore the historic cathedral square or visit picturesque Taormina.

Next, you dock in Valletta, Malta. The UNESCO World Heritage-listed capital is celebrated for its baroque palaces, the grand St. John’s Co-Cathedral, and panoramic views from the Upper Barrakka Gardens. Following a restful day at sea crossing the Mediterranean, the cruise returns to Barcelona on the morning of Day 8.

The Ship

The MSC World Europa is MSC’s flagship and features many attractions on board. The ship is very versatile and can also be deployed in colder regions. However, it specializes in warmer regions like the Mediterranean, the Arabian Peninsula, and the Caribbean. Instead of a single pool deck, the ship features a tiered design with pools and whirlpools on different levels, designed to comfortably accommodate up to 6,774 passengers.

One of the highlights is the split design of the cabin towers. This architecture creates significantly more exterior surface area for balcony cabins. You’ll need to choose whether you want a cabin facing inwards towards the promenade or outwards to the sea. Both have their advantages, depending on whether you prefer to relax or watch the lively activity. This design also creates new spatial concepts for a wide promenade and numerous specialty restaurants (available for an extra charge).

MSC has also packed the ship with attractions. The water park, with its numerous slides and play areas, is complemented by “The Venom Drop @ The Spiral,” a dry slide that descends 11 decks to the promenade. There are also bumper cars, show lounges, aesthetically designed upper decks, and a huge panoramic lounge at the stern of the ship.

The onboard language is English, but the staff speaks several European languages, and the currency used is the Euro.

item.content:encoded:
Currently, Explora Journeys, the luxury brand of MSC Cruises, is offering an interesting cruise from Miami to Reykjavik. The ship departs on May 6, 2028, visiting numerous destinations in the USA and Canada over the course of 22 nights. Currently, the cheapest Ocean Terrace Suite (category OT2) is bookable starting from €11,205 per person. Solo travelers can book this cruise starting from €15,365, representing a surcharge of approximately 37%.

Info

Do you have questions about the offer, need help booking this cruise, or are you looking for a cruise that suits you even better? Feel free to contact us via our inquiry form or WhatsApp. We’re glad to help.

Subscribe to our WhatsApp Channel or Telegram Channel to get instant notifications for all of our best deals!

Included Services

With Explora Journeys, the following services are included in the cruise fare as standard:

  • Full board with all meals, including most specialty restaurants and in-suite dining
  • Selection of fine wines and premium spirits
  • Specialty coffees, teas, and soft drinks (including minibar in the suite)
  • Welcome bottle of champagne in the suite
  • One bottle of wine and one bottle of spirits of your choice in the suite
  • Gratuities
  • 24-hour in-suite service
  • Access to the Thermal Spa wellness area
  • Complimentary shuttle service between the ship and city center (where available)
  • Unlimited high-speed Wi-Fi via Starlink

The following services are available for an extra charge:

  • Anthology specialty restaurant
  • Chef’s Kitchen cooking classes
  • Premium selection of exclusive wines, spirits, and liqueurs
  • Wellness treatments

The Route

Your luxury cruise begins in Miami. If you arrive early, you can take a walking tour to admire the pastel-colored, geometric buildings of the Art Deco District or explore the graffiti murals of the Wynwood Walls. The ship departs in the evening, and you will begin your journey with two relaxing days at sea. This is the perfect opportunity to familiarize yourself with all the amenities and services on board.

The first stop is the global metropolis of New York. The city that never sleeps offers countless attractions, including views of the Statue of Liberty, the neon-lit Times Square, and the towering Empire State Building. Next, the ship heads to Portland, Maine. The lively Old Port district features a sophisticated art scene, and you can sample the world-famous Maine lobster at the fish market or in one of the award-winning local restaurants.

After another day at sea, you will reach Sydney, Canada. Nature lovers can enjoy hiking along the scenic Cabot Trail and taking in the spectacular landscapes. The journey continues via Charlottetown to the Magdalen Islands, where nearly 320 kilometers of beaches await. The landscape here is characterized by picturesque coastal villages and red sandstone cliffs.

Another highlight of this route is the stop in Quebec City, where Parisian-style bistros and contemporary art exhibitions invite you to linger. The historic old town charms visitors with its impressive architecture and landmarks. Passing through La Baie and Sept-Îles, the ship continues to Havre-Saint-Pierre, where an excursion to the Mingan Archipelago National Park Reserve is highly recommended. Further stops in Newfoundland include Corner Brook and L’Anse aux Meadows. After three days at sea, the Explora IV will reach Iceland’s capital, Reykjavik, where your 22-night cruise comes to an end.

The Ship

The Explora IV is currently under construction and is scheduled to enter service in 2027. The vessel will be 267 meters (876 feet) long and 32 meters (105 feet) wide. It will accommodate up to 926 passengers and 640 crew members. This favorable guest-to-crew ratio allows for highly attentive, personalized service. Additionally, the ship is equipped with an LNG propulsion system, underscoring the cruise line’s commitment to sustainability.

Onboard, multiple specialty restaurants offer varied culinary themes. Sakura serves Pan-Asian specialties, while Marble & Co. Grill features dry-aged steaks in an elegant setting. A new addition is the Shore Club on 11 / The Conservatory, a restaurant designed in the style of an exclusive beach club. Guests who prefer not to dine at the restaurants can also choose to have their meals served directly in their suite.

Onboard entertainment includes performances by local artists, karaoke nights, and dance classes. The Helios Pool & Bar area on Deck 12 offers an adults-only retreat. Explora IV also features a spacious spa area for relaxation, alongside a modern fitness center for workouts.

The accommodations on board consist entirely of suites designed for comfort and style. Standard amenities include comfortable double beds, spacious terraces (some featuring private whirlpools), elegant bathrooms, and walk-in wardrobes.

The primary language on board is English. Depending on the destination, the onboard currency is either the Euro or the US Dollar. Any incidental expenses incurred during the cruise can be easily settled using major credit cards.

Below are a few impressions of the ship:

Getting There & Away

The cruise starts in Miami and ends in Reykjavik. Flights for May 2028 are not yet open for booking. A one-way flight to Miami typically costs around €350, and you should plan for about €150 for a return flight from Iceland (excluding checked bags in both cases).

item.content:encoded:
SAS offers special fares for young people under the age of 26. With SAS Youth Fares, you can often save a significant amount on flights to and from Scandinavia. Long-haul flights, for example from Scandinavia to North America, are also cheaper than regular fares.

These fares are particularly attractive compared to standard prices if you want to fly at short notice or during peak travel periods (e.g., during the summer holidays).

Show Deal

Flights to the far north are sometimes relatively cheap with easyJet or Norwegian, but they are often quite expensive. However, if you are between 12 and 25 years old, SAS has a great offer for you. SAS is one of the few airlines in Europe that still offers dedicated fares for young travelers.

Editor’s Note: Few European airlines still offer dedicated youth fares. With SAS Young, you can change your flight without a change fee and only pay the fare difference, which is a big plus for flexible trips to Scandinavia.

Search & Book

SAS Youth Fares can only be booked through this specific SAS landing page. It is important to start your flight search directly via this link. There, you will also find a low-price calendar, which allows you to quickly and easily see when the cheapest flights are available.

The offer has almost no restrictions. There is no minimum stay, no advance booking period, and no expiration date. If there is availability, you can easily book flights for the same day. According to SAS, booking is only possible in booking classes V or O. Your age must be verified with a valid ID at the airport; otherwise, SAS reserves the right to refuse boarding and cancel the flight.

Another advantage is the flexible rebooking policy. Changes to the ticket are possible at any time; you only have to pay the fare difference between the old and new flight. There is no fixed rebooking fee.

Short Haul

Below is an example of flights from Berlin to Copenhagen from December 5 to 12, 2026. The prices are for the SAS Young Light fare and were checked on October 7, 2026:

The SAS Young Light fare only includes a personal item measuring 40x30x15 cm. The SAS Young Standard fare, with an 8 kg cabin bag and a 23 kg checked bag, costs an extra €30 per direction in this case.

On the same travel dates, the cheapest regular fare for these flights would cost €139:

In this example, the youth fare saves you around 17%. Prices stay more or less the same, even at short notice. Of course, not every flight can be booked this way, as some may be sold out or the required booking class may no longer be available. According to SAS, you always save at least 10% compared to the regular fare, and the airline says discounts of up to 70% are possible.

Connecting flights to destinations within Scandinavia are also bookable, although the savings there are usually not as significant.

Long Haul

Youth fares also apply on long-haul routes, though the prices are no longer as attractive as they once were. A 23 kg checked bag is now included again on long-haul flights, because the tickets are issued in the SAS Young Standard fare. A round trip from Berlin to New York for young travelers starts at around €476:

Travelers aged 26 and over would pay €584 including a checked bag in this case. That’s a saving of €108, or around 18%, for young travelers:

It is always worth comparing prices with other airlines before booking. It may be considerably cheaper elsewhere if you only intend to travel with carry-on luggage.

item.content:encoded:
Raffles is one of the most luxurious hotel brands and its hotels are usually extremely expensive. Currently, however, you can book the Raffles Dubai through LuxuryEscapes at a highly discounted price if you stay for at least 3 nights. For only €173 per night (including the local tourism fee), you get a 70 m² Club Room with lounge access, i.e. with breakfast, afternoon tea, and evening cocktails included. That represents savings of roughly 49% compared to booking direct. To get this rate, apply our promo code TDZ10Q426 at checkout for an additional 10% discount. The best rates are available in February and March as well as from June to September 2027.

Info

You don’t necessarily need to decide on specific dates right away. LuxuryEscapes also allows you to lock in the price and redeem the voucher you get later, subject to availability. To do that, click on Buy now, choose dates later under the big Check Availability button.

Show Deal
Info

The legal drinking age in the United Arab Emirates is 21. The hotel charges a tourism fee of AED 20 (~€5) per room per night. It is paid locally at the hotel, but for transparency we have already included it in the deal price.

Cancellation Policy

Luxury Escapes’ cancellation terms are a bit complex. A full refund to your original payment method is only available up to one week after booking. Otherwise, the following applies:

  • Up to 7 days after booking: free cancellation (provided you cancel at least 14 days before arrival)
  • Up to 46 days before arrival: cancellation possible, refunded as Luxury Escapes credit
  • From 45 days before arrival: non-refundable

Your booking includes a guaranteed upgrade from a Signature Room to a Raffles Club Room. You also get 20% off food and drinks at all bars and restaurants, 20% off laundry service, and either early (from 10:00) or late (until 16:00) check-in/out, subject to availability. There’s also an AED 100 (~€24) spa credit per package, but it comes with a minimum spend of AED 400 (~€97).

Breakfast is served at the Azur Restaurant on the third floor. Between 14:00 and 16:00, you’ll be served a selection of pastries, scones and sandwiches in the Raffles Club Lounge. Between 18:00 and 20:00, the lounge will offer evening canapes, a light buffet dinner, cocktails and mocktails.

The room is a whopping 70 m² large, featuring e.g. a balcony, a bathtub, a desk, a TV, and WiFi, among other things. You can choose if you prefer a king bed or twin single beds. The room additionally also has a sofa bed.

Editor’s Note: Even cheaper than last time: for €173 per night you get a 70 m² Club Room with breakfast and Club Lounge access including afternoon tea and evening cocktails – roughly half of what ALL Accor members pay for the same room when booking direct.

The Hotel

The Raffles Dubai is an Egyptian-inspired posh 5-star hotel, located a short drive away from the Dolphinarium. As usual for Raffles Hotels, it offers a butler service. The property also boasts a swimming pool.

Previous guests left very good reviews of the hotel (e.g. 4.7/5 on Google or 5/5 on Tripadvisor), many praising the respectful staff, the historical interior, the extensive breakfast buffet, the luxurious spaces, the evident security, the impeccable cleanliness, the comfortable pool, the superb spa area, and the amazing views of the Khalifa. The hotel also seems to be very popular among honeymooners. There doesn’t seem to be a single aspect that has received any major criticism.

Located in Bur Dubai, you’re close to the famous Dubai Frame. You can find both elegant boutiques and discount stores in the hotel’s vicinity and the Zabeel soccer stadium is also nearby.

The hotel is also conveniently located only about 7 to 10 kilometers from Dubai International Airport. Depending on traffic and terminal, the drive by car or taxi usually takes just 9 to 15 minutes. The Dubai Metro takes around 35 to 40 minutes and is the cheapest option.

Price Check

For our price check, we picked a 3-night stay from February 22 to 25, 2027. Booking through LuxuryEscapes, you currently pay €173 per night (including the local tourism fee and our 10% coupon) for the Club Room with breakfast and lounge access.

Info

These dates fall during Ramadan, which is also observed in the United Arab Emirates. Expect some restrictions in public life, which may also affect the availability of alcoholic drinks in the Club Lounge. That said, the restrictions have been relaxed considerably compared to the past.

By comparison, booking the same Club Room with breakfast for the same dates on the hotel’s website costs €1,016 (around €339 per night), and that’s already the member rate for ALL Accor. So you save around 49% by booking through LuxuryEscapes and also get extras such as the spa credit and early check-in or late check-out. Long story short: the savings are big!

Oneworld member Royal Jordanian has been offering a status match to its Royal Club program for a while now. Notably, you can even get Oneworld Ruby with just a hotel status. Those with a frequent flyer status at another airline (Gold or similar) are matched all the way up to Oneworld Sapphire.

It’s worth noting that this is not a challenge but a genuine status match. The benefits are guaranteed for 12 months after the match, without you ever having to set foot on a Royal Jordanian plane.

Show Deal
Update

From November 1 to 7, 2026, the following offer applies:

  1. If you hold a hotel status (Accor Gold, Hilton Gold, IHG Gold, Marriott Gold, Radisson Premium), you can buy Oneworld Sapphire for US$149 (~€132).
  2. Everyone else only needs a free Radisson Rewards account (= Club tier). That also gets you Oneworld Sapphire, for US$248 (~€220). Or Oneworld Ruby for US$49 (~€44).

The regular status match for members of other frequent flyer programs is still available for US$149 (~€132) as well.

Tip

Already used the Royal Jordanian match in the past and no longer eligible? There is also a status match to Malaysia Airlines Enrich (e.g. for Miles & More members). Oneworld Sapphire costs US$199 (~€177) there, though.

However, there’s a catch: the provider statusmatch.com handles the process and charges the following fees:

Technically, StatusMatch.com requires at least an entry-level hotel status to use the match. Besides Marriott Silver, IHG Silver and the like, a Radisson Rewards Club account also qualifies – and you get one simply by signing up for free. The full list of which status is matched to what is in the FAQ. Residence in the following countries is required: Austria, Bahrain, Belgium, Canada, Cyprus, Denmark, Egypt, France, Germany, Iraq, Italy, Jordan, Kuwait, Lebanon, Netherlands, Oman, Portugal, Saudi Arabia, Spain, Sweden, Switzerland, Syria, Turkey, UAE & the United Kingdom.

Editor’s Note: Until November 7, a free Radisson Rewards account is all you need to buy a full year of Oneworld Sapphire – alliance-wide lounge access plus a guest for US$248 (~€220), or US$149 (~€132) if you already hold a Gold-level hotel status.

Programs Eligible for Matching

A comprehensive list of eligible programs can be found in the FAQ on the Status Match website. For Europeans, the most notable include Flying Blue, Miles & More, Emirates Skywards, Etihad Guest, SAS EuroBonus, TAP Miles&Go, and Turkish Miles&Smiles.

Airline Loyalty Programs

The benefits only get really interesting from Gold Sparrow (= Oneworld Sapphire) with alliance-wide lounge access. For that, you need US$149 (~€132) and one of the following statuses:

  • Air Canada Aeroplan: 50K / 75K / 100K
  • Air Europa Suma: Gold / Platinum
  • Egyptair Plus: Gold / Platinum / Elite
  • Emirates Skywards: Gold / Platinum
  • Etihad Guest: Gold / Platinum / Emerald
  • Flying Blue: Gold / Platinum / Ultimate
  • Gulf Air Falconflyer: Gold / Black
  • Kuwait Oasis Club: Gold / Platinum
  • MEA Cedar Miles: Gold / Platinum / Pres. Club
  • Miles & More: Senator / HON Circle
  • SAS EuroBonus: Gold / Diamond / Pandion
  • Saudia Alfursan: Gold
  • TAP Miles&Go: Gold / Navigator
  • Turkish Miles&Smiles: Elite / Elite Plus
  • Virgin Flying Club: Gold
  • WestJet Rewards: Gold / Platinum

Hotel Loyalty Programs

Until November 7, 2026, hotel status also gets you Oneworld Sapphire. The fee is US$149 (~€132) if you hold one of the following statuses:

  • Accor ALL: Gold and above
  • GHA Discovery: Platinum and above
  • Hilton Honors: Gold and above
  • World of Hyatt: Explorist and above
  • IHG One Rewards: Gold Elite and above
  • Langham Hotels: Diamond and above
  • Marriott Bonvoy: Gold Elite and above
  • Meliá: Gold and above
  • Preferred Hotels: Gold and above
  • Radisson Rewards: Premium and above
  • Shangri-La: Jade and above
  • Wyndham Rewards: Platinum and above

Don’t have any of these statuses? Then simply sign up for Radisson Rewards for free. You’ll instantly get Club status, which lets you match to Oneworld Sapphire for US$248 (~€220).

Alternatively, you can get Oneworld Ruby for US$49 (~€44), although its benefits are limited.

Travel Credit Cards

Holders of eligible credit cards can also take part, but only get Oneworld Ruby – for US$49 (~€44). You need one of the following cards:

  • Visa: Signature / Infinite
  • Mastercard: World / World Elite
  • American Express: any Amex card

Cards/members from the following countries are eligible: Bahrain, Belgium, Canada, Cyprus, Denmark, Egypt, France, Germany, Iraq, Italy, Jordan, Kuwait, Lebanon, Netherlands, Portugal, Qatar, Saudi Arabia, Spain, Sweden, Switzerland, Syria, Turkey, United Arab Emirates and the United Kingdom. Austria is not on the list.

Status Benefits

On RJ.com, you can find a full overview of Royal Club benefits. Here are the key highlights:

Silver Jay (Oneworld Ruby)

The Silver Jay status corresponds to Oneworld Ruby. Beyond that, there are hardly any notable benefits, even on Royal Jordanian flights:

  • Business class check-in on Oneworld flights
  • Free Preferred seats (with exceptions)
  • Extra baggage allowance and priority boarding with some airlines (e.g. American Airlines)
  • Priority on waitlists and standby
  • No mileage expiration

Gold Sparrow (Oneworld Sapphire)

Gold Sparrow is the sweet spot, equivalent to Oneworld Sapphire. It gets you into business class lounges on every Oneworld flight, as long as there is one at your departure airport:

  • Lounge access: business class lounges with one guest when flying Oneworld (with a few exceptions, e.g. the Qatar Airways business lounges)
  • Priority boarding: board with business class passengers
  • Seats: free extra-legroom seats with some airlines
  • Extra baggage: additional weight or an extra piece (excluding some “Light” fares)
  • Priority baggage: your bags are among the first on the carousel
  • Fast track: faster immigration on arrival in Jordan
  • No mileage expiration

Note: the annual business class upgrade voucher that regular Gold Sparrow members get is not included with the status match.

Process

The process is relatively self-explanatory once you’ve created an account. Here’s a summary of the steps:

1. Create a Royal Club Account

To participate, you need an account with Royal Jordanian’s frequent flyer program, Royal Club. You can create one for free at the following link:

Sign up at the Royal Club

After registration, your frequent flyer number will be displayed, which you’ll need for the next step:

2. Apply for a Status Match

After noting your frequent flyer number, proceed to the actual status match on rj.statusmatch.com:

Status Match

Next, you’ll need to specify your current frequent flyer status. Then you’ll be asked for proof, which can be a physical frequent flyer card or a screenshot from your online account.

Only then will you see which status you’ll actually receive. For a Miles & More Senator, for example, this would be Gold Sparrow = Oneworld Sapphire:

3. Pay

As described above, the fee for Oneworld Ruby status is US$49 (~€44). For Gold Sparrow (= Oneworld Sapphire) status, the fee is US$149 (~€132), or US$248 (~€220) when matching from an entry-level hotel status or a free Radisson account.

Payment is by credit card only. A decision on the match takes up to 5 working days, after which the status is valid for 12 months.

Extending Status

Royal Jordanian used to require a certain number of segments (2 to 20) on its own flights each year to earn or keep a status. That’s now history. To extend your status, all you need is:

  • Silver Jay (Oneworld Ruby): 12 Oneworld segments within 12 months
  • Gold Sparrow (Oneworld Sapphire): 26 Oneworld segments within 12 months
  • Platinum Hawk (Oneworld Emerald): 80 Oneworld segments within 24 months
Warning

Readers have reported several times that segments were not credited as expected, even after contacting customer service. So don’t expect everything to work smoothly.

However, only flights that earn at least one mile count. Depending on the airline, some discounted booking classes may be excluded. Generally, eligible Iberia flights can be found for as little as €20 per segment.

If you are not using the status match, initial qualification follows a slightly different set of requirements:

Find more details in the following post:

Conclusion

While the trend of charging fees for status matches (via statusmatch.com) is frustrating, Royal Jordanian offers a direct path to status without requiring a “challenge” of actual flights.

The current offer is especially interesting if you’re new to airline status: being able to simply buy a meaningful status like Sapphire beats any mileage run. With lounge access for two and possibly extra baggage, the US$149 (~€132) or US$248 (~€220) fee pays for itself after just a few flights. Even the US$49 (~€44) Ruby match is a solid deal if you mainly want to skip check-in queues and get better seats.

Info

With this deal, you will be booking a 36 to 41 m2 Superior Room for the price of a Standard Room.

LuxuryEscapes Cancellation Policy

LuxuryEscapes offers a rather complicated cancellation policy. It basically comes in three steps:

  • Until 7 days after booking: You get a full refund in your original form of payment, as long as you cancel at least 14 days before arrival. This is the last chance to get your money back.
  • Over 22 days before your stay: You can get a full refund in the form of LuxuryEscapes credit. You won’t get your money back, but can use it to book a different hotel on LuxuryEscapes.
  • Less than 21 days before your stay: You won’t get a refund in any form if you cancel or no-show.

Editor’s Note: About €131 per night for a superior room at a 5-star hotel with breakfast, daily spa access and dining credit is hard to beat in Budapest, and it’s around 37% less than the same dates on other booking sites.

The Hotel

Kozmo Hotel Suites & Spa is a luxurious 5-star hotel housed in a beautifully restored historic former telephone exchange building. It is known for its excellent service, spacious and quiet rooms and large bathrooms with deep bathtubs. This hotel is perfect for a romantic city break in the Hungarian capital. After a day of exploring, recharge in the spa before venturing out again to discover more of the city’s charms.

The superior rooms are elegantly designed in calming colors and come with a king-size bed, a small seating area and a desk. Some rooms also have a walk-in closet.

The wellness center features a stylish indoor pool, a whirlpool, a fitness center and treatments by the spa brand Valmont. With this deal, you can use the spa for 60 minutes per day at no extra cost. The €25 dining credit (per stay, not per person) can be used at the Bistro. You can check the menu here.

Previous guests have left excellent reviews of the hotel (e.g. 4.7/5 on Google and 4.9/5 on Tripadvisor). They rave about the spacious rooms, attentive staff and luxurious amenities.

The hotel is located in a quiet part of Józsefváros (8th district), near the Grand Boulevard (Nagykörút) and just minutes from Kálvin tér metro station. It’s slightly outside the main tourist center, but many sights along the Danube are within a longer walk or a short ride on public transport. The airport is about 19 km away, which takes 35 to 55 minutes by taxi or bus 100E, depending on traffic.

item.content:encoded:
The Costa Smeralda is the second-newest ship in the fleet of the Italian cruise line Costa. This winter, she will sail to the Canary Islands, Madeira and Morocco. Before that, she repositions from Savona in Italy to Tenerife, departing as early as November 12, 2026.

If you have flexible dates and want a last-minute break, this sailing is currently very cheap. It departs on Thursday, November 12, 2026, and you can book 11 nights in an inside cabin from just €549 per person with full board and tips included. Oceanview cabins start at €649 per person, while balcony cabins are available from €849 per person (based on double occupancy). Solo travelers can book an inside cabin from €824, which is a 50% single supplement.

Info

Do you have questions about the offer, need help booking this cruise, or are you looking for a cruise that suits you even better? Feel free to contact us via our inquiry form or WhatsApp. We’re glad to help.

Show Deal

Subscribe to our WhatsApp Channel or Telegram Channel to get instant notifications for all of our best deals!

What’s Included

With Costa, the following services are included in the cruise fare by default:

  • Full board with all meals in the main dining room and buffet restaurant (specialty restaurants at an extra charge)
  • Water, tea and coffee at breakfast, plus water in the buffet restaurants during opening hours
  • Gratuities
  • Use of most onboard facilities (gym, pool area incl. sun loungers, etc.)

Costa includes water, tea and coffee at breakfast in the main dining room and in the buffet restaurant during its opening hours. In the main dining room and in all specialty restaurants, you pay for every drink, including water. That makes a drinks package more worthwhile with Costa than with other cruise lines. You can book drinks packages in advance and pay for them via MyCosta until 48 hours before departure.

Costa offers the following optional drinks packages:

Drinks Packages at Costa
  1. MySoft Drinks package
    From €23 per person per day, children aged 4–17 pay €15 per day.
    Includes unlimited non-alcoholic drinks by the glass:
    • Coffee & tea
    • Soft drinks
    • Energy drinks
  2. MyItalian package
    €34.30 per adult per day, children aged 4–17 pay €15 per day (non-alcoholic). Already included if you book the All Inclusive fare.
    Includes:
    • Tea, coffee incl. cappuccino, water, soft drinks and more
    • Draft beer, aperitifs and cocktails (except solid, molecular and premium drinks)
    • A selection of wines, spirits and liqueurs
    • One bottle of water (0.5 liters) per person per day (adults only), ideal for shore excursions
    • Unlimited ice cream (max. 2 scoops per order)
    • One free pizza per cruise at the Pummid’Oro pizzeria (excluding “Gourmet” pizzas)
  3. MyItalian Plus package
    €45.80 per adult per day, children aged 4–17 pay €15 per day (non-alcoholic). Already included if you book a suite on the All Inclusive fare.
    Everything in the MyItalian package plus:
    • Molecular and premium cocktails
    • Bottled Corona and Beck’s
    • Unlimited bottled water (0.5 liters)
    • Minibar drinks
    • Looza fruit juices

There are also packages with a fixed number of drinks, e.g. 20 glasses of beer (0.4 l) for €105 (€5.25 per glass) or 13 bottles of mineral water (1 l) for €42 (€3.23 per bottle). You can also book these packages before your cruise via MyCosta.

Editor’s Note: For around €50 per day with tips included, this repositioning cruise packs Marseille, Barcelona, Málaga, Cádiz, Gran Canaria and Madeira into one trip. It also arrives in Tenerife a day before disembarkation, giving you an extra day on the island.

The Route

The cruise begins in Savona in northern Italy. If you arrive early or the day before, you can visit the Priamar Fortress with its views over the sea, the Torre del Brandale (the landmark of the old town) and the Cathedral of Nostra Signora Assunta with Savona’s own Sistine Chapel. The ship leaves port at 5:30 pm.

The first stop is Marseille. Highlights include the Old Port (Vieux-Port) with its morning fish market and Notre-Dame de la Garde, the basilica on the city’s highest point with 360° views. A stroll through Le Panier, the oldest quarter, is also worth it.

Next up is Barcelona. A shuttle bus run by the port takes you from the terminal to the Columbus Monument at the end of La Rambla. Don’t miss the Sagrada Família, but book your tickets online in advance. Other popular spots are the Gothic Quarter with its cathedral and La Rambla with the La Boqueria market.

After a sea day, the ship arrives in Málaga. The old town is about a 15-minute walk from the port. Art lovers should visit the Picasso Museum. Alternatively, you can take a day trip to the Alhambra in Granada. It’s about 90 minutes each way, so it’s best booked as an excursion through the cruise line. The next stop is Cádiz, where the ship docks right next to the old town. The Andalusian city has a cathedral with a golden dome, the Torre Tavira lookout tower and the Mercado Central, which has a large selection of fish and seafood.

On day 8 you reach Gran Canaria. The ship stays until 8 pm, which leaves time for plenty of options. You can spend a relaxed day at Las Canteras, the city beach, explore the old town of Vegueta with the Santa Ana Cathedral, or take a tour to the Maspalomas dunes in the south. The next stop is Funchal on Madeira, the “island of flowers”. The ship only arrives in the afternoon, so focus on the city itself. Take the cable car from Funchal up to Monte and ride back down in one of the famous wicker toboggans. The botanical garden is also worth a visit.

The cruise ends after 11 nights in Tenerife. The Costa Smeralda arrives on Sunday, November 22, a day before disembarkation, so you have time for excursions there too. We recommend San Cristóbal de La Laguna, a UNESCO World Heritage city about 20 minutes away by tram. You could also visit the Anaga Mountains with their laurel forests or Las Teresitas beach. Disembarkation is after breakfast on Monday, November 23, 2026.

The Ship

The Costa Smeralda was launched in 2020 and carries up to 5,200 passengers. She has a gross tonnage of 182,000 and measures 337 meters long and 36 meters wide, with a draft of 8 meters. She has 18 decks and was built at the Meyer Turku shipyard in Finland for around US$950 (~€844).

The ship has 15 restaurants, including Chinese and Japanese options. Six are included in the cruise fare (main dining rooms and buffets). Three are reserved for suite guests, club members or families. Six premium venues are available for an extra charge and offer better food in a more exclusive setting.

At the stern on deck 7, there’s an outdoor bar with plenty of seating and a great view of the sea. This includes three cozy round lounges that are lit up in the colors of the Italian flag in the evening.

We especially recommend the aft balcony cabins, as some of them have much larger balconies than the cabins along the sides. On longer cruises in warm regions, this is a real advantage: some aft balconies even have room for a sun lounger.

The Colosseo is the ship’s central meeting point, spanning three decks with several bars. Our pick there is the Ferrari Bar, whose signature cocktails are only served at that bar. The same goes for the Campari Bar.

Here are some photos of the cabins and the ship:

Across the public decks, there are 19 bars as well as a cinema, theater, shopping center, casino, pool deck (with a covered pool for cooler days), fitness center, water slide, disco, aqua park and kids’ club.
